If it still holds fuel.|The dock worker|}} A [[Mon Calamari]] '''dock worker''' worked at a port on the [[Water|estuary]] [[moon]] of [[Trask]]. The dock worker watched the [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]]'s [[gunship]] the ''[[Razor Crest]]'' descend to the surface and fall into the water. After Djarin came out, the Mandalorian employed the Mon Calamari to make repairs to his ship, paying one thousand [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]]. The dock worker did a patchwork job and repaired the [[sublight engine]]s, and when Djarin returned he was displeased with the work. The Mon Calamari ultimately made Djarin agree to the repairs on a [[datapad]]. ==Biography== {{Quote|So, how can I help you?''"
"''Can you fix it?''"
"''Fix it? Nah. But I can make it fly.|The dock worker and Din Djarin|}} During the [[New Republic Era|reign]] of the [[New Republic]], the [[Mon Calamari]] worked as a dock worker at a black market port on the [[Water|estuary]] [[moon]] of [[Trask]]. In [[9 ABY]],{{MandoDate|11|the appearance of the [[Mon Calamari]] dock worker}} the dock worker was present at a launchpad at the port when the [[gunship]] ''[[Razor Crest]]'' entered Trask's [[atmosphere]] at high speed, plummeting towards the surface. The Mon Calamari witnessed the ''Crest'' falling and catching fire, before rapidly decelerating before the launchpad to make a swift landing. One of the gunship's [[sublight engine]]s then malfunctioned and the ''Razor Crest'' swerved into the sea beside the launchpad, prompting a shaking head from the dock worker. [[File:DjarinSignsForRepairs-TMCh11.png|thumb|left|300px|The dock worker was hired by Din Djarin to make repairs to the ''Razor Crest'']] After the ''Razor Crest'' was carried onto the launchpad by a [[heavy industrial crane transport|Trask walker]], the gunship's [[pilot]] and owner, the [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Din Djarin]], came out and was greeted by the dock worker. The Mon Calamari asked what help was required, and Djarin asked back whether the dock worker could fix the ''Crest''. The dock worker replied that the gunship could be made to fly again, and so the Mandalorian gave him thousand [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] to do make whatever repairs were possible. Mon Calamari verbally decided to fuel the ''Razor Crest'', but showed skepticism on whether the gunship could still hold fuel. The Mon Calamari got to work on the ''Razor Crest'', patching up [[hull]] breaches, repairing the engines and leaving netting and lines within the cockpit. When Djarin returned, he was dissatisfied with the work, remarking that he had given the dock worker a thousand credits. The dock worker then reached a [[datapad]] out for the Mandalorian to consult regarding the commission of the repairs. Djarin complied and agreed to the repairs before departing on the ''Crest'', which took off very shakily. ==Personality and traits== The Mon Calamari dock worker had [[Color|brown]] skin and orange [[eye]]s. The dock worker gave a shaking head upon seeing the ''Razor Crest'' fall into the ocean. The Mon Calamari was doubtful about being able to entirely fix the gunship, showing skepticism on whether the vessel could still hold fuel. After Din Djarin complained on the quality of the dock worker's work, the worker proceeded to show the Mandalorian to a datapad to agree to the repairs. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|I gave you a thousand credits, this was the best you could do?|Din Djarin, to the dock worker|}} The dock worker specialized in repairing vehicles like the ''Razor Crest'', although his work on the gunship did not entirely satisfy Din Djarin, who had to receive further repairs on the [[planet]] [[Nevarro]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}} ==Equipment== The Mon Calamari [[Clothing|wore]] a blue sweater with a black overall over it which had white straps and outlines. The dock worker also had a brown [[belt]] with compartments and used a datapad. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|This is Mon Calamari. It's for episode 203. This is Frank Ippolito inside. He is the craftsman, and the costumes are authentic wools that we've over dyed and stained and aged.|Costume designer Shawna Trpcic|{{DisneyGallery|Disney Gallery: The Mandalorian: Making of Season Two|Making of Season Two}}}} [[File:DisneyGallery-FrankAndShawna.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Frank Ippolito in costume as the dock worker with Shawna Trpcic (right), the designer of the character's clothing]] The Mon Calamari dock worker appeared in "[[Chapter 11: The Heiress]]" of [[Jon Favreau]]'s [[2019]] [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', directed by [[Bryce Dallas Howard]] and released on [[November 13]], [[2020]].{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-november-2020|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in November 2020}} Credited as "dock worker" in the subtitles, he was played by the costume's craftsman [[Frank Ippolito]], with [[Janina Gavankar]], who played [[Iden Versio]] in ''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'', serving as one of two puppeteers.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/mandalorian-janina-gavankar-battlefront-2-cameo?sf132475121=1|text=Star Wars: Battlefront 2's Janina Gavankar Reveals Secret Cameo in The Mandalorian|author=Kim, Matt T.M.|date=2020-11-14|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]|quote=Where's Janina?|archivedate=20201130010744}} The character made a brief cameo appearance in a market on the planet [[Tao]] in the ''[[Star Wars: Visions]]'' short film "[[Lop & Ochō]]."{{Visions|Lop & Ochō}} Ippolito created the Mon Calamari's headpiece and, because it took two puppeteers to animate it, he asked Gavankar to handle the nostrils when a second one was required. The Mon Calamari's clothing was designed by costume designer [[Shawna Trpcic]] and made from authentic wools which had been over dyed, stained, and aged to make it look vintage like. Following the release of "Chapter 11: The Heiress," the dock worker received attention over [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] over the Mon Calamari's sweater.{{WebCite|url=https://mashable.com/article/the-mandalorian-mon-calamari-sweater/?europe=true|text='The Mandalorian' births a new internet STAR: Mon Cal in a sweater|author=Gallucci, Nicole|date=2020-11-15|work=Mashable|quote=Beloved internet stars Baby Yoda and Chris Evans now have some serious competition: A Mon Calamari in a sweater.|archivedate=20201116081725}} ==Appearances== *[[The Mandalorian Season 2 Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian Season 2'' Junior Novel]] *[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 2|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 2]] *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 11: The Heiress}} {{1st}} *[[The Mandalorian Season 2 3|''The Mandalorian Season 2'' 3]] ===Non-canon appearances=== *{{Visions|Lop & Ochō}} ==Sources== *{{SW|url=news/mon-calamari-holiday-sweater-cookies|text=Fix Yourself Some Mon Calamari Holiday Sweater Cookies}} *{{DisneyGallery|Disney Gallery: The Mandalorian: Making of Season Two|Making of Season Two}} *{{InsiderCite|219|A Certain Point of View (department)}} ==Notes and references== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of unidentified Mon Calamari dock worker}} {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |es=Trabajador portuario mon calamari no identificado |fr=Ouvrier portuaire Mon Calamari non identifié |ja=名称不明のモン・カラマリの港湾労働者 |ka=დოკის უცნობი მონ კალამარი მუშა |pl=Kalamarianin (Trask) }} [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Mon Calamari]]
